historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (7.9%) tempered to 7.0% for year 1: store count is flat, FY2026 growth of 9.0% came from online and +2.4% SSSG, and the outlook describes a 'rational' consumer
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.0% exceeds revenue 5yr CAGR 7.9% by 39% -- equity is inflated by the RMB245.7m Jan-2026 placing and by retained earnings on a ~70% payout; revenue is the right growth anchor. EPS 5yr 8.2% agrees with revenue.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series reported FCF - SBC - interest income (FY2021 1,159.4; FY2022 630.1; FY2023 709.4; FY2024 1,362.9; FY2025 867.1; FY2026 1,122.2; all RMB m). Lease cash is not in the Metrics history before FY2025 so the CAGR series is pre-lease; FY2026 post-lease owner FCF is 785.9 and FY2025 is 551.1. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR is -0.7% against +0.4% reported because SBC rose 16.5 -> 68.4 (4x) while FCF was flat on FY2021's working-capital-boosted base; FY2021 and FY2024 were working-capital release years and FY2025 a build year, so the 3yr figure (16.5%) overstates the trend as much as the 5yr understates it. Base growth is anchored on revenue, not FCF.

scenario_narratives.base: JNBY compounds as a mature 2,100-store designer-brand platform: revenue +7% in FY2027 fading to 3% by FY2034 (5yr revenue CAGR 7.9%, FY2026 +9.0% with flat stores), pre-SBC IFRS-16 EBITDA ~29.5%, lease cash ~5.5% of sales, capex front-loaded at 5.5% for the Shuangpu park then ~3%, 26% cash tax. Owner-FCF margin (post-lease) ~11% in the park years rising to ~14% at maturity, against 13.0% actual in FY2026.
scenario_narratives.bull: The H2 FY2026 re-acceleration (+11.6%) persists: policy-supported consumption recovers and the K-shaped market concentrates share in head designer brands; online (24% of revenue, +20.5% in FY2026) and the emerging brands (+32%, 8% of revenue) keep compounding, members with >RMB5k annual spend grow ~9%/yr, multi-brand formats and the Box Project lift store productivity, and the owned park trims rent -- 10% growth for two years fading to 3.5%, EBITDA to 31%, terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: A renewed consumption downturn, which the data already hint at (H1 FY2026 offline SSSG -2.2%; NBS clothing sales negative in Aug-2026): revenue +2% then -1%/0% before a 2% crawl, the 54%-of-revenue JNBY flagship stalls before the emerging brands are large enough to matter, 166-day inventory forces markdowns and provisions, and S&M (36.0%) and rent deleverage on flat sales -- EBITDA compresses to 26%, lease ratio to 6%, terminal growth 2%. Net cash and the ~70% payout mean no solvency question; the downside is a de-rated, ex-growth cash cow that still has to build the park.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the owner cash flow of a high-gross-margin (66.6%), net-cash, high-payout Chinese designer-apparel group on a strict basis: SBC expensed, lease cash charged in full (treatment B), interest and fair-value gains stripped with their assets put back in the bridge, the already-paid post-year-end dividend removed from cash, and a 15x terminal cap so the result does not depend on a re-rating the HK market has never granted (stock at ~10x P/E). Scenario weights, not a WACC premium, carry the China consumer risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Chinese discretionary consumption: FY2020 and FY2022 both saw revenue fall; a repeat is the bear case, and the 25% bear weight is a judgment.
Flat store count: growth now depends on SSSG, online mix and younger brands; CROQUIS (-25 stores) and jnby by JNBY (-8) shrank in FY2026.

Rent and S&M ratio creep: selling & marketing rose to 36.0% of revenue; lease cash is 5.6% and ~RMB675m of total lease outflow sits in the P&L -- under treatment (B) a 1pp lease-ratio move is ~RMB60m of annual owner FCF.
Park capex: construction scope beyond the contracted 37% of the site is unquantified; the model assumes ~RMB400m incremental over FY2027-29.
Governance / related parties: HQ and retail premises leased from chairman-related Huizhan/Huikang; VC-fund stakes are related to a NED; founder family controls the company.
FX: CNY flows against an HKD quote -- a 5% CNY move is ~HK$1.7/share of value; fx_rate is dated 2026-10-22 and is not refreshed by price-only updates.
Dividend policy: payout ~70% plus the 10th-anniversary special; the valuation does not assume the special recurs.
Government grants (RMB66m, ~5% of PBT) are treated as recurring operating income; their withdrawal would cost ~RMB0.09/share of annual FCF.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY: 10-yr CGB ~1.8% + China equity risk premium incl. country risk ~7.2% x beta ~1.0 = ~9.0% cost of equity; rounded up to 9.5% for a founder-controlled HK-listed mid-cap with related-party HQ/retail leases. Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. Same 9.5% in all three scenarios -- cyclicality and consumer risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate (charge-risk-once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease-liability cash payment (RMB336.4m FY2026 = principal + RMB25.9m interest, 'Payment of lease liabilities' in financing; total lease cash outflow note 14 RMB675.6m less RMB338.6m short-term/variable rent already in opex) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (5.56% of revenue). Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (117.0 PPE + 11.2 intangibles = 128.3m, 2.12%; ROU depreciation 308.8m excluded). ebitda_margin_path is the pre-SBC IFRS-16 EBITDA margin (op profit 1,333.9 - FVTPL fair-value gains 62.1 + D&A 437.1 + SBC 68.4 = 1,777.2m, 29.4%).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (RMB46.7m book, -0.5m share of FY2026 profit). Flows are consolidated; the NCI book value is deducted once in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: Chinese designer-brand apparel group -- JNBY, CROQUIS, jnby by JNBY, LESS plus emerging brands; 2,118 standalone stores, ~24% self-operated, 80%+ of retail sales from members). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US/consumer' with the adaptations file: dual currency (CNY flows / HKD quote), IFRS-16 leases (treatment B), small NCI, and the matching-asset rule (interest income on cash/deposits stripped from flows, VC-fund and financial-product fair-value gains stripped from EBITDA, the matching assets added in the bridge). Owner FCF FY2026 = reported FCF 1,230.9 - SBC 68.4 - interest income 40.2 - lease cash 336.4 = 785.9m (13.0% of revenue); the component build reproduces ~797m for FY2026, a 1.4% tie. Post-balance-sheet: the FY2026 final HK$1.06 + special HK$0.75 dividend (RMB0.93 + 0.66) was paid 16 Oct 2026 on ~523.7m dividend-bearing shares; the price is ex-dividend, so RMB832.7m is deducted from the 30-June cash in equity_bridge. Capex is lifted to 5.5% of revenue for FY2027-28 and 4.5% FY2029 for the Shuangpu 'modern park' (203k sqm land use right RMB309m obtained July 2025; construction contract on 37% of the site signed April 2026, completion end-2028, internally funded); maintenance capex ~3.0-3.3%. Scenario axes drawn from 3306.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-22) and the FY2026 annual report MD&A/outlook: China discretionary demand (H1 FY2026 offline SSSG -2.2%, full-year +2.4%; NBS clothing retail sales -0.5% nominal YoY in Aug-2026), online mix (24% of revenue, +20.5%) versus offline (+5.8%), younger/emerging brands (+32% off an 8% base) against a 54%-of-revenue JNBY flagship, S&M ratio creep (36.0%) and inventory days (166), and the multi-year park capex.
inputs.guidance_note: No numeric FY2027 guidance. Outlook (AR p.29): consumer confidence 'stabilized' but spending 'rational'; K-shaped divergence favouring head brands; strategy is portfolio optimisation (self-incubation or M&A), member operations, omnichannel. FY2026 revenue +9.0% (H1 +7.0%, H2 +11.6%), offline SSSG +2.4%, store count flat (2,117 -> 2,118), active members 560k -> 610k, >RMB5k members 330k -> 360k.

bear.narrative: Chinese discretionary spend rolls over again (FY2020/FY2022 pattern): negative SSSG, distributor destocking, CROQUIS/jnby by JNBY store closures continue, discounting and inventory provisions cut gross margin while S&M and rent ratios deleverage on flat sales -- EBITDA settles at 26%, ~3.4pp below FY2026; the park is still built, so capex is not avoided.

base.narrative: Growth decelerates from 7% toward 3% as the store base stays ~2,100 and growth comes from SSSG, online mix and the younger brands; EBITDA margin held ~29.5% (S&M ratio creep from online offset by gross-margin stability at ~66-67%); lease cost eases 0.2pp once the owned park takes warehousing in-house; capex front-loaded for the park then ~3%; cash tax 26% = 25% PRC statutory plus 5% dividend withholding on a ~70% payout (FY2026 ETR 26.4%, cash 23.7%); working capital consumes 10% of incremental revenue (FY2026: ~-20%; FY2024 release).

bull.narrative: H2 FY2026's +11.6% pace holds: consumption recovery plus K-shaped share gain for head designer brands, member base compounding (>RMB5k members +9%/yr), online and the Box Project scaling, LESS and emerging brands offsetting CROQUIS; operating leverage on a 66.6% gross margin lifts EBITDA 1.6pp; owned park trims rent.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the business is a pure play on Chinese mid-to-high-end discretionary spending, the store base is no longer growing, two of three 'younger' brands lost stores in FY2026, and the company itself describes consumers as 'rational' and 'cautious' on non-essentials. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs both a macro recovery and continued share gain to hold double-digit growth from a flat footprint. No solvency or refinancing risk (net cash RMB1.5bn pre-dividend), so bear is a margin/growth case, not a survival case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
